title: Two Coins for the Ferryman
description: THE VELVET HEARSE, "Two Coins for the Ferryman" (an imaginary record): the house combo of a funeral home, 1971. Funeral chime, a polite theme, a drum break the drummer could not resist, a sung chorus, a 7/8 crossing, stop-time, two hot choruses and an unresolved ferryman chord.

sections.development: the viewing-room bell alone; Odile breathes in and sighs one note; the bowed saw and the clock
the theme politely: reed, voice, Rhodes tines, vibes, bass, conga tones; no drum kit
the drums alone, one late snare, a conga roll
the whole band; Odile doubles the reed an octave down in the last bar
kit out; the theme sung over bass and vibes, a scat run, a long fall
eight cycles of 7/8 (2+2+3): vibes riff turning metallic, hands, log, saw, bell, the impossible voice, reed barks
two stabs, silence, the bass alone on low F
feral reed with one overblown note, cries; then reed and voice in unison, a chromatic climb
the ferryman chord, unresolved; the bell; two coins; a breath out
